_comment: TEMPLATE — not read by app.js. Copy to site_profile.json, fill it in, and only then wire the engine to it. Canonical definition: 'Lookup Tool — Design Specification.md' §2A; worked example and the antibody tiers it drives: 'Group 2 — … Diagnostic Pathway.md' §2.6 and §7.7. Every value below is a placeholder, NOT a claim about any laboratory. A profile that overstates what a laboratory can do is worse than no profile at all: it makes the tool offer nodes the site cannot answer and lets the registry record a confident answer that was really a guess.
_status: UNDECLARED. Group 2 Diagnostic Pathway §9.3 lists declaring this as the one outstanding item that genuinely blocks the site-adaptive behaviour. Until it is declared and the engine reads it, the four rules in Design Specification §2A are NOT in force: every node is offered, and a test the laboratory cannot run is answered 'not done' by the abstractor and carries a provisional_pending. That is honest but noisier than it needs to be.
_engine_rules_awaiting_declaration: 1. A node whose required test is not in the profile is never offered; it resolves to its nos_fallback with a provisional_pending naming the missing test. Needs both this file AND a per-node capability declaration, which no group's dt.json carries yet.

2. endemic_context feeds prior_probability. Group 2's nodes already carry prior_probability values authored for a high-EBV, high-TB, high-HIV, HTLV-1-low setting; declaring the profile is what makes those values a property of the site rather than a hard-coded assumption.
3. imaging and protocols gate the staging and behaviour questions — above all 9751, where no PET-CT means extent_unknown rather than an inferred answer.
4. fixation gates every IHC and FISH tier.

_tier_reference._comment: Pathway §2.6 states the antibody guidance as capability tiers, not as a shopping list, and no tier is 'wrong' — a Tier 1 site producing correct family-level codes is doing better than a Tier 3 site producing confident wrong ones. Listed here so whoever fills in ihc_available can see which codes each addition unlocks.
